title: A group of jinn listened and were amazed.
subtitle: Unseen listeners at a dawn prayer
then: The introduction relates from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet ﷺ led Fajr at Nakhlah while travelling with Companions. {idea}A company of jinn passed, stopped, and listened attentively.{/idea} Allah told him ﷺ to inform his people that {idea}the jinn believed and affirmed it.{/idea}
now: You have heard the same surahs in every Taraweeh since you were a child. They play in the background while you cook. {idea}Some listeners hear it once and are stunned.{/idea} When did you last let it amaze you?
old: I know the Quran already. It is familiar background.
new: The Quran is wondrous. Familiarity is the only thing dulling it.
try: Listen to one short surah today as if hearing it for the first time.

title: It guides to what is right, so we believed.
subtitle: Hearing, recognising, committing
then: The jinn did not debate. Ibn Kathir says right course means {idea}what is correct and leads to success.{/idea} They heard, saw the guidance in it, believed, and promised {idea}we will never associate anyone with our Lord.{/idea}
now: You hear a reminder that hits you at a friend's wedding, a funeral, a random clip online. You think: that is true. Then you scroll on. {idea}The jinn heard and acted in the same breath.{/idea}
old: Agreeing with a reminder is enough.
new: When guidance rings true, the right reply is a commitment.
try: Take one line of Quran that moved you recently and act on it today.

title: Our Lord is too exalted for a wife or son.
subtitle: The jinn's first lesson about Allah
then: Ibn Abbas said Jadd means {idea}His actions, commands and power{/idea}, and also His blessings on creation. Mujahid said it is His magnificence. When the jinn believed, {idea}they declared Him far above taking a spouse or a child.{/idea}
now: It is natural to imagine Allah the way we imagine a powerful person: moods, needs, family. {idea}The jinn's first realisation was that He is nothing like that.{/idea} He needs nothing. Everything needs Him.
old: I picture Allah somewhat like a very powerful person.
new: Allah is exalted beyond anything I can compare Him to.
try: Read Surah Al-Ikhlas slowly today and reflect on each line.

title: Our fool used to say outrageous things about Allah.
subtitle: Realising who had been misleading them
then: Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and As-Suddi said the foolish one meant {trap}Iblis.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds it includes anyone who claims Allah has a spouse or son. Hearing the Quran, the jinn saw their old leader for {trap}what he was.{/trap}
now: There is always a voice that sounds sure of itself: a podcast host, a loud uncle, an influencer with a theory about God. {idea}Confidence is not the same as truth.{/idea}
old: If someone speaks confidently about religion, they probably know.
new: Anyone who says things about Allah without knowledge is foolish, however sure they sound.
try: Before sharing anything about Allah today, check its source first.

title: We never imagined anyone would lie about Allah.
subtitle: How trust kept them misled
then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {trap}we did not think humans and jinn would join together in lying about Allah.{/trap} So they believed it. {idea}When they heard the Quran, they knew it had been a lie.{/idea}
now: A forwarded message in the family group: a hadith with no source, a story about a miracle. You assume no one would make that up about religion. {trap}People do.{/trap}
old: Nobody would invent things about religion, so what I hear must be true.
new: Even religious claims need checking. The Quran is the measure.
try: Next time a religious forward arrives, verify it before believing or sharing.

title: Seeking refuge in jinn only made the fear grow.
subtitle: Turning to the wrong protector
then: Ibn Kathir says pre-Islamic Arabs entering a valley would say: {trap}I seek refuge with the master of this valley.{/trap} Seeing their fear, the jinn {trap}increased them in fear and terror{/trap} and grew bolder against them. Ikrimah said the jinn had feared humans until then.
now: The lucky charm in the car. The horoscope you check before a big day. The fortune teller your aunt swears by. {trap}Every false shelter feeds the fear it promised to calm.{/trap} Seeking refuge belongs to Allah alone.
old: A little superstition is harmless and makes me feel safer.
new: Turning to anything but Allah for protection only grows the fear.
try: When you feel uneasy somewhere today, say a'udhu billah and mean it.

title: They thought, as you did, that no messenger would come.
subtitle: Giving up on guidance arriving
then: Al-Kalbi and Ibn Jarir said they thought {trap}Allah would never send a messenger after such a long time.{/trap} The jinn were telling their people they had shared the same mistake as the humans of Makkah.
now: You have been asking for guidance on a decision for months and feel nothing. Or you feel far from Allah and think it is too late for anything to change. {reward}Guidance came after centuries of silence. It can reach you too.{/reward}
old: It has been so long, guidance will not come to me now.
new: Allah sends guidance after long silences. It is never too late.
try: Make istikhara or a sincere dua for guidance on one decision today.

title: We reached for the sky and found it guarded.
subtitle: The heavens sealed when revelation came
then: Ibn Kathir says when the Quran was revealed, Allah {reward}filled the sky with stern guards{/reward} so devils could not steal from it and pass it to soothsayers. He did this {reward}out of kindness and mercy to His servants{/reward}, protecting His Book.
now: The Quran you scroll past on your phone was protected at the level of the sky. {idea}Allah guarded it so carefully because it matters that much.{/idea} The least we can do is open it.
old: The Quran is just one book among many.
new: Allah guarded the heavens to keep this message pure. It is that precious.
try: Open a mushaf today and read one page, slowly.

title: We used to eavesdrop. Now a flame waits.
subtitle: The old shortcut to hidden knowledge was closed
then: The jinn used to sit in places near the sky to steal a hearing. Ibn Kathir says now {trap}whoever tries finds a flame waiting in ambush{/trap}. Soothsayers had mixed stolen scraps with lies, so that {trap}no one knew who was truthful.{/trap}
now: The app that predicts your week. The psychic hotline ad. The friend who reads coffee cups. {idea}The door to hidden knowledge was closed when the Quran came.{/idea} What is left is guesswork.
old: Some people really can see what is coming.
new: The unseen belongs to Allah. Every shortcut to it was shut.
try: If you use any app or habit that predicts your future, delete or drop it today.

title: Is harm meant for earth, or guidance?
subtitle: Good manners even when speaking of the unknown
then: Ibn Kathir notes the jinn's {idea}good manners in phrasing{/idea}: they did not attribute evil to anyone, but {reward}attributed the good to Allah.{/reward} He cites the Prophet's ﷺ words: {idea}and evil is not attributed to You.{/idea}
now: Something hard happens and the first words out are "why is God doing this to me?" The jinn, facing something frightening, still chose their words carefully. {idea}How you speak about Allah in hard moments matters.{/idea}
old: When bad things happen, it is fair to say Allah did this to me.
new: Good is named to Allah. In hardship, I speak about Him with respect.
try: Next time something goes wrong today, say alhamdulillah ala kulli hal before anything else.

title: Some of us are righteous, some not. Many paths.
subtitle: Honesty about their own community
then: The jinn admit their own kind is divided. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said it means {idea}among us are believers and among us are disbelievers.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they were on many differing paths, with different thoughts and opinions.
now: Your family, your mosque, your friend group: it is easy to assume being part of it makes you fine. {idea}Every community has people on different paths.{/idea} The question is which path you are on.
old: Being part of a good community means I am on the right path.
new: Every group has many paths in it. I have to choose mine.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: which path am I on, not which group.

title: We cannot escape Allah, not on earth, not by running.
subtitle: Recognising there is nowhere to hide
then: Ibn Kathir explains their words: {idea}we know Allah's power is decisive over us{/idea}, and even if we try to flee, He has complete control. This certainty was part of what moved them to believe.
now: You change cities, jobs, friend groups, phone numbers. The guilt comes with you. {idea}You cannot outrun Allah, but you can run to Him.{/idea} That is the only direction that works.
old: If I keep busy enough, I can avoid facing Allah.
new: There is no running from Allah, only running to Him.
try: Stop for two minutes today, sit still, and turn to Allah about one thing you avoid.

title: We heard the guidance and believed. No loss to fear.
subtitle: The security of the believer

key.label: What the believer need not fear

then: Ibn Kathir says the jinn were proud of believing, and {reward}it was something worth being proud of.{/reward} Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said the believer need not fear {reward}that his good deeds will be reduced, or that he will carry more than his own sins.{/reward}
now: You give in secret and wonder if it counted. You pray when tired and wonder if it was enough. {reward}Allah does not shrink your reward or add to your load.{/reward} Nothing you do for Him is lost.
old: My small good deeds probably do not count for much.
new: Nothing good I do is lost, and I carry nothing that is not mine.
try: Do one small good deed today and trust it is fully counted.

title: Those who submit have sought out the right way.
subtitle: The just and the unjust among them
then: Ibn Kathir says the Qasit is {trap}one who behaves unjustly with the truth and deviates from it{/trap}, the opposite of the one who is just. Those who submit {reward}sought salvation for themselves.{/reward}
now: Choosing to pray on a work trip, to turn down the deal that is a bit dishonest. It can feel like giving something up. {reward}The verse calls it searching for the right way{/reward}, and finding it.
old: Submitting to Allah means losing things I want.
new: Submitting is how I find the right way and save myself.
try: Make one choice today purely because it is what Allah wants.
